OT-2 Parts Trainer

What you would actually need to build a liquid handler, using the OT-2 as reference — and, because the real goal is materials synthesis, which open-source rig to build instead. Opentrons publishes no bill of materials and no hardware licence, so every row here is tagged with where it came from. The 3D model below is Opentrons' own reference STL, segmented into the same subsystems as the parts list; anything drawn that is not in that STL says so.

The machine, from Opentrons’ reference model

Drag to orbit · scroll to zoom · shift-drag to pan · hover a part for its subsystem and size · click to isolate it, click empty space to show all. Segmentation is by connected body and position in the STL — the deck is one body, the frame ten, the two pipette mounts are the hangers reaching down toward the deck, and the 4,405 remaining bodies at gantry height (mostly fasteners) are motion. Control electronics are not in the STL at all; the boxes drawn in the base cavity are placed by hand and tagged derived.

documented design files exist in Opentrons/ot2 derived inferred — not verified choice you decide, criterion given

The deck, redrawn at 1:1 from the DXF

The file is called CNC_DECK_RevA2.DXF, and the repo notes called it a cut file. Reading the geometry says otherwise: it is a dimensioned drawing sheet at 1:6.5 — B-size title block, zone letters, SCALE: 1:6.5, SHEET 1 OF 2. Send it to a laser as-is and you get a deck 74 mm wide. Below is the plan view scaled back to full size; hover for millimetres.

The open-source rig to build for materials synthesis

An OT-2 moves liquids between SBS plates. Materials synthesis needs that plus stirring, heating, powder or viscous handling, and a path to characterisation. Three open-hardware routes were checked on 2026-09-14; one of them reuses the OT-2’s best part.

Recommendation

Build a Science Jubilee, and put an OT-2 pipette on it.

Jubilee is a tool-changing gantry — a 3D printer that swaps tools — with an MIT-licensed lab automation layer that already ships an OT-2 pipette tool, syringe tools and cameras, a Python/Jupyter API, and a six-plate labware deck. The Pozzo group ran a full sol–gel SiO2 synthesis campaign on it with in-line SAXS (Digital Discovery, 2025), which is the exact shape of a materials workflow. And because the pipette is an OT-2 pipette, the Stage-0 accuracy gate above transfers unchanged: pass it on the bench, then mount the same pipette on a machine that can also hold a syringe, a sonicator, a camera and a heater.

Source: github.com/Opentrons/ot2 — 13 PCB folders, a deck drawing and STEP/STL reference models. No BOM, no LICENSE file. The reference models exist so you can design hardware that integrates with an OT-2, not so you can build one. The 3D view above is the “Detailed” STL (42,172 faces, 4,418 bodies), quantised to 0.01 mm and segmented by cad/segment_reference_model.py; it is not a mechanism model — belts, bearings and pulleys are absent or simplified in the source.
Better starting point if the goal is a working OT-2 clone: Opentrons/otone_hardware (OT.One) — simpler, and it does publish 3D models and a bill of materials. Software stack is Apache-2.0 and genuinely open, unlike the hardware.
